_doc: Own.NET#317: the optional 1-based `column` on the finding-anchor path.
Findings this fixture yields, all carrying a column: the contract param that
became an owned obligation (30:26), two direct acquires (40:13 and 40:44), the
acquire nested in an `if` branch (44:21 - the hoisted path, the one most easily
missed), the subscription (12:17) and the disposable field (21:9).
The two acquires SHARE line 40 and differ only in column: that pair is what
proves the column discriminates rather than decorating every record with the
same number - without it in the dedupe key they collapse into one finding.
`alias_join` and the fresh-returning call result also mint handles that carry a
column; neither yields a finding HERE (the alias shares its source's obligation
and the callee is not known-fresh). Both are covered at Finding level in
tests/test_ownir_column.py instead, where the alias case pins the observed
behaviour: it anchors at the source acquire, never at the alias site.
